primitives.name: Empty Set Definition
primitives.verbatim_quote: It makes for tremendous simplification in language and notation to admit into the class of sets a set containing no points, which we shall call the empty set and denote by 0.
primitives.assumptions: The existence of a unique set with no elements, denoted by $\emptyset$, is assumed as a foundational construct.
primitives.breakdown_regime: No breakdown; the empty set is well-defined for any universal set.

layer2.mapping: In GSI, the empty set corresponds to an impossible event with zero probability. In GSE, it represents an absorbing state with no outgoing transitions.
layer2.telemetry: Verify that empirical data never contains elements outside the universal set.

primitives.assumptions: Two sets are equal if and only if they share precisely the same elements; this is the fundamental criterion for set identity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when there exists at least one element that belongs to one set but not the other.

primitives.name: Class of Sets Definition
primitives.verbatim_quote: To help keep the notions clear, we shall always use the word class for a set of sets.
primitives.assumptions: A class is a collection whose elements are themselves sets; the term distinguishes higher-order structures from simple point sets.
primitives.breakdown_regime: No inherent breakdown; however, Russell's paradox highlights limitations on arbitrary class formation within naive set theory.

layer2.mapping: In GSI, a class of events forms a sigma-algebra. In GSE, a class of states constitutes a partition of the state space.
layer2.telemetry: Ensure that each element of the class is indeed a valid set before further analysis.
